query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

per_column.name: crew_professionalism_assessment
per_column.rationale: A 4-level categorical read of crew behaviour (exceptional/professional/indifferent/rude) that partly overlaps the original numeric 'Staff Service' rating, but adds a qualitative axis (distinguishing rude_dismissive from merely indifferent) that is genuinely useful for exploring which aspects drive sentiment. Values are well distributed, not near-constant. Grounding is mostly sound: samples 1,3,4,5 cite explicit crew praise ('very kind & helpful', 'well-trained on hospitality', 'showcased friendly culture') that supports the label. However sample 2's review is entirely about seats/entertainment and says NOTHING about crew, yet the operator asserts 'indifferent_careless' — an invented negative value on a silent row, which is a hallucination rather than a legitimate 'unknown'.

per_column.name: seat_physical_comfort
per_column.rationale: Categorises seat experience (comfortable/adequate/cramped/broken). Overlaps the original 'Seat Comfort' rating, capping novelty, but the categorical nuance (esp. 'broken_defective') and the large NULL share (3384) show it correctly abstains when seats are unmentioned — good behaviour. Groundedness is strong: sample 1 ('legroom is spacious')→comfortable_spacious, sample 2 ('far too narrow, poor padding')→cramped_uncomfortable, sample 5 ('comfortable and wide')→comfortable_spacious all match. Only mild stretch is sample 3 (only 'aircraft well-maintained' → adequate_acceptable) and sample 4 labelling a full 3-3-3 economy cabin 'comfortable_spacious', but these remain reasonable readings, not fabrications.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: This is largely a categorical restatement of the already-present 'Value For Money' rating column, so it adds little new analytical leverage for THIS exploratory query. Groundedness is the weaker dimension: value/price is rarely stated in the text, and the operator repeatedly infers a specific monetary verdict from generic positivity — sample 4 ('excellent_value') and samples 1 & 5 ('good_value') come from reviews that never mention cost or worth. It does correctly return 'Unknown' on sample 2, showing it can abstain, but the confident specific-value inferences on silent rows are unwarranted.

per_column.name: service_consistency_reliability
per_column.rationale: Unlike the other three, reliability/consistency (and the 'declining' bucket) is NOT captured by any original column, so it supplies a genuinely new axis — useful for the analyst deciding which aspect to study. Grounding is mixed: sample 5 ('service was consistently good from start to finish') is a textbook match, and samples 3/4 are defensible inferences from broadly positive descriptions. But 'consistency' judged from a single flight is a stretch, and sample 2 (a seat/entertainment complaint with no service content) is labelled 'poor_unpredictable' — an assertion the source does not support.

judge.rationale: For an open-ended 'which aspect is most worth analyzing' query, decomposing free-text reviews into per-aspect categorical labels is a sensible move and the values are well-spread rather than constant. However, three of the four columns (crew, seat, value) shadow existing structured rating columns (Staff Service, Seat Comfort, Value For Money), so their marginal analytical leverage is limited — value_for_money_perception in particular is close to a restatement. service_consistency_reliability is the standout because it introduces a reliability/decline dimension absent from the originals. On groundedness, seat and crew are mostly sound and the operator does abstain (NULL/Unknown) on many silent rows, which is correct behaviour; but there is a recurring failure to abstain in aspect-silent reviews — sample 2 fabricates negative crew and service-consistency verdicts, and value_for_money infers specific monetary judgments from mere overall positivity. Net: moderately useful with partial redundancy, and moderately grounded with a real pattern of over-asserting on silent rows.
